rules.decision: Prefer an exact small-sample procedure over an asymptotic two-proportion or chi-square approximation when a 2x2 independent table is sparse.
conditions: Large-sample approximation assumptions are not satisfied
rules.action: Consider Fisher exact test and do not rely on an ordinary chi-square or z approximation solely because the table is 2x2.
warnings: Do not use expected-count thresholds mechanically without considering the exact table structure and analysis objective.
exceptions: For larger RxC tables or complex survey/clustered data, use a method appropriate to that structure rather than automatically applying 2x2 Fisher exact.

source_evidence.support: NIST identifies Fisher Exact Probability Test as an exact nonparametric option for two small independent samples in a 2x2 table.
Penn State states that Fisher's exact method may be used when normal-approximation assumptions for two independent proportions are not met.

rules.decision: Use a rank-based two-sample procedure as an alternative when independent-sample mean-comparison assumptions are unsuitable and the estimand matches a distributional/location comparison.
conditions: Research question concerns a between-group location/distribution difference
rules.action: Consider Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney U rather than forcing a t-test when parametric assumptions are not defensible.
diagnostics: Distribution shape when interpreting as a location shift
warnings: Do not automatically interpret the test as a difference in medians unless the relevant distributional conditions justify that interpretation.

source_evidence.support: Ott and Longnecker present the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a nonparametric alternative for two independent population central values and note equivalence to Mann-Whitney U.

rules.decision: Use a paired rank-based method when paired-data parametric assumptions are unsuitable and a rank-based paired comparison matches the question.
conditions: Research question concerns within-pair change or difference
rules.action: Consider Wilcoxon signed-rank as a nonparametric paired alternative.
warnings: Do not analyze paired observations as independent groups.

source_evidence.support: Ott and Longnecker present Wilcoxon signed-rank as a nonparametric alternative for paired data.

rules.decision: Use one-way ANOVA only when comparing mean responses across more than two independent groups under an appropriate one-factor model.
conditions: One categorical grouping factor with more than two levels
rules.action: Consider one-way ANOVA and assess model assumptions before relying on F-test inference.
assumptions: Approximately normal errors within groups for standard small-sample inference
diagnostics: Normality diagnostics when sample sizes are small
warnings: Do not use ordinary one-way ANOVA for repeated, clustered, or otherwise dependent observations.
exceptions: If parametric conditions are unsuitable and a rank-based comparison fits the question, consider Kruskal-Wallis.

source_evidence.support: The text describes one-way ANOVA assumptions and emphasizes independence as the most critical condition.

rules.decision: Use Kruskal-Wallis as a nonparametric alternative for comparing more than two independent groups when ANOVA conditions are unsuitable.
conditions: Research question concerns a between-group distribution/location difference
rules.action: Consider Kruskal-Wallis instead of forcing one-way ANOVA.
diagnostics: Distribution shapes if interpreting results as location differences

source_evidence.support: The text presents Kruskal-Wallis as the nonparametric alternative in the chapter on comparing more than two population central values.
NIST lists Kruskal-Wallis for comparing several populations with unknown distributions.

rules.decision: A causal question must pass an explicit identification gate before Methodome recommends a causal estimator.
conditions: User/protocol seeks an effect, impact, intervention effect, or other counterfactual contrast
rules.action: Require a defined intervention/exposure, outcome, target population, causal estimand, and defensible identification assumptions before method selection.
assumptions: Exchangeability or a design/strategy that justifies the relevant exchangeability condition
warnings: Do not convert an ordinary observational association model into a causal claim merely by adjusting for covariates.
Causal identification and statistical estimation are separate problems.
exceptions: Randomized assignment changes the identification argument but does not remove the need to define the estimand and analysis population.

source_evidence.support: Hernán and Robins organize observational causal identification around exchangeability, positivity and consistency, and explain that randomization is expected to produce exchangeability.

rules.decision: Difference-in-differences requires a defensible equal/parallel trends assumption and should not be suggested from before/after data alone.
conditions: Treated and comparison groups observed over time
Program assignment is not simply individual randomization
rules.action: Consider difference-in-differences only when the design supports a credible comparison group and the equal-trends assumption is addressed.
assumptions: Equal/parallel untreated outcome trends across groups over the relevant pre-intervention period
No design violations that invalidate the comparison
warnings: A pre/post comparison without a credible comparison group is not difference-in-differences.

source_evidence.support: World Bank guidance gives difference-in-differences its own chapter and explicitly identifies the equal-trends assumption and method limitations.

rules.decision: Primary analysis variables and their operational definitions should be prespecified before outcome-driven analysis decisions.
conditions: A protocol/SAP defines primary and secondary objectives or outcomes
rules.action: Capture primary versus secondary status, operational outcome definition, analysis population, and planned analysis before locking the Methodome plan.
diagnostics: Check whether primary-variable definition changed after data review
warnings: Post-hoc redefinition of a primary variable can introduce bias and multiplicity problems.

source_evidence.support: ICH E9 states that the precise primary-variable definition should be specified in the protocol and warns against post-hoc redefinition.

rules.decision: Methodome analysis plans should separately record analysis sets, missing-data handling, estimation/testing, multiplicity, subgroup/covariate plans, and sensitivity analyses where applicable.
conditions: An analysis plan is being created or locked
rules.action: Represent these elements explicitly rather than burying them in free text.
warnings: A method name alone is not a complete analysis plan.
exceptions: Not every project requires every field; applicability should follow design and objectives.

source_evidence.support: ICH E9 Section V treats these as separate data-analysis considerations.
Gamble et al. provide a minimum-content framework for SAPs aimed at transparency and reproducibility.
